Is this true and is it a problem from your perspective? The new review-time pipeline can report outdated review-time values after a normal extract run that omits --include-comments, because previously stamped PRs remain marked as covered
  even though their thread data was not refreshed. That is a correctness issue for the new metrics.

  Review comment:

  - [P1] Invalidate old review-time coverage when skipping --include-comments — E:\projects\ado-git-repo-insights\src\ado_git_repo_insights\cli.py:762-765
    When extract runs without --include-comments, this branch deliberately leaves existing comments_extracted_at values untouched for PRs that were refreshed in the current run. If one of
    those PRs received new approvals or thread changes since the last thread-enabled extraction, _generate_weekly_rollups() will still include its old review_time_minutes because it only
    checks comments_extracted_at IS NOT NULL. In that common incremental-update scenario, the patch silently publishes stale review-time metrics for already-covered PRs instead of
    suppressing them until comments are refreshed again.

**Title:** feat(#217): review time pipeline — extract, aggregate, and display P50/P90 metrics

**Body:**

## Summary

- Add review_time extraction from ADO PR thread system comments (vote events), computing earliest-approval-to-creation-date duration per PR
- Aggregate review_time_p50/p90 into weekly rollups and all 6 dimension slices (author, repo, team, reviewer, cross-dims), gated on per-PR comment coverage completeness
- Schema migrations v1→v2→v3→v4: add review_time_minutes, comments_extracted_at, PR-scoped thread identity with composite PK, backfill coverage markers
- Regenerate 260-week demo dataset with realistic review_time values (30-70% of cycle_time)
- Bump AGGREGATES_SCHEMA_VERSION 2→3 across Python, TypeScript, and manifest

### Key design decisions
- **review_time derived solely from pr_comments**, not the stale reviewers table (ADO never deletes removed reviewers)
- **Convergence**: clear-then-repopulate within a transaction on every recompute; withdrawn approvals correctly produce NULL
- **Coverage gating**: aggregation SQL CASE filters on per-PR `comments_extracted_at IS NOT NULL`, preventing partial-fetch data from entering rollups
- **Post-close approvals dropped** (SC-002): votes after PR closure would exceed cycle_time

### Review session fixes (final commit)
- **C1 (CRITICAL)**: `upsert_pull_request` changed from `INSERT OR REPLACE` to `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE`, preserving `review_time_minutes` and `comments_extracted_at` across re-extraction
- **H1**: Transaction wrapper around `populate_review_timestamps` clear-then-repopulate
- **H2**: Boundary tests for `_ROLLUP_MIN_SAMPLE` threshold and p50<=p90 invariant
- **D1**: `validate_manifest_addressability` now skips gitignored files (dev-ex fix for any developer who has run the real pipeline)

## Test plan

- [x] 1616 tests passing (1612 cross-platform), 84.6% coverage
- [x] `python scripts/run_pr_preflight.py` green (all gates)
- [x] Pre-commit hooks clean
- [ ] CI pipeline passes
- [ ] Dashboard loads with review_time cards visible in demo data
- [ ] Verify `--include-comments` extraction populates non-null review_time values

Closes #217
